video_title: Clippers Falllout: ESPN reporter defends ESPN report on Steve Ballmer?

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: ESPN's report on Steve Ballmer's alleged funneling of money to Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: the NBA had found no evidence Steve Ballmer funneled money through aspiration to Kawhi Leonard
quotes.quote: We reported that the NBA had found no evidence Steve Ballmer funneled money through aspiration to Kawhi Leonard. The Watchell report confirmed this. It did not identify direct evidence and that allegation was not a central focus. I am sorry, I must be living in La La Land. The 35-page report from Watchell specifically has the evidence that money was funneled from Steve Ballmer to Aspiration. Specifically it is in there, with evidence, 50 million dollars worth of legal fee evidence.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: ESPN's report on the Clippers' introductions of Dennis Robertson
quotes.excerpt: the NBA's investigation was focused on the Clippers' introductions of Kawhi Leonard's representative Dennis Robertson
quotes.quote: We reported that the NBA's investigation was focused on the Clippers' introductions of Kawhi Leonard's representative Dennis Robertson, you know him as Uncle Dennis. The introductions of Dennis to team sponsors and whether those interactions constituted salary cap circumvention. That issue became a primary focus of the report. I read that from Don Van Natta and I said, uh-oh, I better go read the report again, because there is no way that the report I read from Watchell has this as the primary focus.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The rule against paying players outside of their team salary
quotes.excerpt: when you pay a player, you can't give him anything other than what he gets
quotes.quote: When you pay a player, you can't give him anything other than what he gets every two weeks from the team. That's the rule. If you're giving a player anything outside of that, you better disclose it and you better make sure that you count it towards your salary cap. Whether it's a private plane, whether it's a sponsorship with one of your companies, it doesn't matter. The rule is simple and we all know it, even Lawrence Frank. Any money outside of the every other week paycheck, it counts.
